clue.text: Bad temper shows when many people get away

parts.note: meat or game that has gone off is said to be high
to temper food is to season it, as with salt

explanation.surface: A tetchy mood is on display at the time crowds go off on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad temper' reads as one idea, irritability, but it splits in two: game that has gone off is called high, and to temper food is to flavour it.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak holiday period is the stretch of the year when most travellers take their trips.

clue.text: Choice of meal, we're told

indicators.note: the phrase says the word that follows is heard, not seen, so take its sound

parts.note: meal is coarsely ground grain, another word for flour

explanation.surface: A diner is told what options there are on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meal' looks like food on a plate, but it is ground grain, FLOUR, which sounds like the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group, its finest part, is called its flower, as in the flower of youth.

clue.text: Very few otherwise caught by double blow

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, as a ball is caught in hands

parts.note: a one-two is a boxer's quick pair of punches
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll be late'

explanation.surface: A boxer's combination punch lands, though rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' signals a container. A one-two is the boxing term for a pair of punches thrown in quick succession.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a couple of things means a small handful, hardly any at all.

clue.text: Satisfied after batting is not cut short

indicators.note: one piece is placed following the other, so the word for batting comes first

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
having eaten enough, one is full

explanation.surface: A cricketer has had their fill after an innings that lasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' signals that the word for 'Satisfied' follows the word for 'batting'; in cricket the team batting is said to be in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given completely, with nothing omitted or abridged, is given entire.

clue.text: Might discover number available

explanation.surface: Someone may find out how many there are on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb but is the noun for power; the second sense is a unit's full complement, as in a regiment at full strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is power or force; the headcount a team or army can call on is also its full complement.

clue.text: Navigate estuary from which river emerges

annotationWithheld.why: Navigate estuary from which river emerges (4) for TEES: 'Navigate' gives STEER, and taking out R leaves STEE, not TEES; no parse found and no reprint or blog gives another reading.
annotationWithheld.clue: Navigate estuary from which river emerges

clue.text: Wish to leave

explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' looks like departing, but here it means leaving something to an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire or intent is one sense; the other is to bequeath property in a testament.

clue.text: Also included in mild reproof occasionally

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as an item is included in a set

parts.note: 'now then' is said as a gentle telling-off
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Gentle telling-off is given from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' signals a container. 'Now then' is a mild British rebuke, like 'come on now'.
explanation.definitionFit: From time to time, at irregular intervals rather than regularly.

clue.text: Certainly self-confident?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: a person lacking doubt is sure of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is undoubtedly, for sure; read literally, the phrase describes someone free of any doubts about themselves.

clue.text: Appear, and love being in club's musical

parts.note: to show up is to appear

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, so the zero sits within the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport; the 's is no letter
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone turns up, keen to join the society's stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' puts O, love as nil in tennis, inside BAT. Show Boat is the 1927 Kern and Hammerstein musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is a famous stage musical about performers on a Mississippi river steamer.

clue.text: A continental facility causing concern

parts.note: un is the French masculine word for 'a'
facility in the sense of ease, doing something without effort

explanation.surface: A European amenity is giving rise to worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facility' looks like a building or service, but it means ease of action. 'continental' points to French, where 'a' is UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Worry or anxiety is a feeling of disquiet.

clue.text: Reportedly, Gulf road leading to capital

indicators.note: the word signals that what follows is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a gulf is a bay and a road is a route, together bay route

explanation.surface: Word is that a highway along a Middle Eastern gulf runs to the seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulf road' gives BAY ROUTE, which said aloud matches the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the seat of government of Lebanon.

clue.text: Pledge to help out a tenor

indicators.note: the helping word stands out, around the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: to oblige someone is to help them out
T is the standard abbreviation for tenor in choral scoring

explanation.surface: A promise to assist a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'help out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' tells you OBLIGE goes outside A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind oneself by a promise or duty is to commit, as to a debt or task.

clue.text: About to rustle up culinary delicacy

indicators.note: about means round and about, scattered, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of preparing a fancy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' is the anagram signal for TO RUSTLE UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A soup made from the meat of a sea reptile was a prized Victorian luxury dish.

clue.text: He chose Carl to put off educationalist

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed, thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A man picks Carl to postpone a meeting with an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like postponing, but it tells you to shuffle HE CHOSE CARL TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A classroom instructor is someone whose profession is education.

clue.text: Upkeep?

parts.note: read as 'up keep', a stronghold standing high on a rise of ground rather than maintenance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Upkeep' means maintenance, but split it: a keep is a castle's stronghold, and this one is up on high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient fortified settlement on a summit is literally a keep set up high.

clue.text: Total accepted as satisfactory

parts.note: the total is all of it
right means correct, the accepted answer

explanation.surface: The whole sum is approved as adequate.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay, acceptable, good enough.

clue.text: Pointless burning note though angry

indicators.note: the compass point south, S, is dropped from the word

parts.note: something burning is in flames
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A burning note sent in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' removes S, a compass point, from IN FLAMES, leaving IN FLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A temper that has been stirred up is heated, as in inflamed passions.

clue.text: Academic noblewoman making complaint

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree, so it stands for an academic
a lady is a woman of noble rank

explanation.surface: A titled scholar is lodging a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance, but here it means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment or illness.

clue.text: Court painter holding nothing against pretty woman

indicators.note: one piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was principal painter to Charles II's court
O is zero, nothing
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A royal portraitist, with nothing to set against it, paints a beautiful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O and V inside LELY, the 17th-century portraitist at the English court.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, the word is informal for an attractive woman.

clue.text: Vehicle US prosecutor left after exposing criminal

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is placed following the prosecutor

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
a DA is a district attorney, the US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: An American prosecutor's van is left behind once a crook is unmasked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places L behind DA, the US district attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wilfully damages property is an offender against the law.

clue.text: Just dread tailing Libya's leader

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first, as one tails behind another
a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: dread as an adjective means terrible or awful

explanation.surface: Fear follows the head of the North African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'only', but it means fair. 'tailing' sets AWFUL behind L, the first letter of 'Libya's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and permitted by the rules, legitimate.

clue.text: Suffer from hard-hearted master

indicators.note: a piece put at the heart of another goes into its middle

parts.note: an ace is a master of some skill
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough-minded expert is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard-hearted' looks like callous, but it says put H, hard, at the heart of ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt dully and persistently, as a sore limb does.

clue.text: Bandsman?

parts.note: a band here is a body of workers joined together, so a member of one, not a musician

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bandsman' suggests a musician, but a band can be any group banded together, like a trade body.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a trade association of workers belongs to an organised group.

clue.text: Bank on escape from London area

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece sits on, or before, the next

parts.note: a shore is the bank of a sea or lake
to ditch something is to get away from it, abandon it

explanation.surface: Someone banks on getting out of a part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank on' reads as 'rely on', but 'Bank' is a synonym and 'on' puts it first in an across answer. Shoreditch is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a district in the East End of the British capital.

clue.text: Australia's only border

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for Australia, as in A$ for its dollar; the 's is no letter
but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: The country's sole frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to lie next to.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjoin, sharing an edge with something.
